title: scaling_report: report a binned spatial transcriptomics scaling exponent so that two sections can be compared
description: Computes the pooled noise-resolution exponent of binned spatial transcriptomics from the mean and variance of per-bin counts, then states what a test that assumes Poisson would actually do at each bin size. Reports the per-gene distribution, the effective number of genes behind the pooled number, and the range of per-gene medians the same pooled value admits. Version 1.1 adds a reader that takes a Space Ranger output folder directly (--from-10x), so the user no longer has to write the multi-scale aggregation; a single-file HTML report with two figures and a per-scale table; a seven-check end-to-end self-test (--selftest); and a synthetic-data demo with an exponent known by construction (--demo). Reproduces the colon section shipped in examples/ (gamma_pool = 0.5547, IGKC 87.7% of the exponent). At 256 um the implied false-positive rate is 72% on section P1 and 78% on P2, the index section; values are medians over the 2,000 most abundant genes, which is the definition the accompanying manuscript uses. Accompanies the manuscript 'Binning in spatial transcriptomics removes two- to twenty-fold of the excess variance, not the sixteen-thousand-fold that counting statistics predict' (submitted). Python >= 3.9, numpy only. Version 1.2.0 adds reproduce/02_OUT/numbers_v8.json, the single file from which every number in the manuscript is written, together with the three scripts that generate it and render the manuscript (a missing key stops the build). Version 1.3.0 adds the calibration that the revised manuscript reports: the measured false-positive rate of a Poisson test and the power kept by a quasi-likelihood test at each bin size, with the three scripts that produce it, their outputs, and the two eight-scale moment tables they read. numbers_v8.json grows from 209 to 284 keys; nothing was removed. Version 1.4.0 ships package 1.2.0, which adds the quasi-likelihood correction itself (ql_test, ql_z, ql_p) rather than only the calibration that prices it.
